choice_reason: 1. B's plan-differences table restructures into legible stacked label/value blocks at the required 390px viewport (verified in state-03-390-px-viewport.png and the max-width:640px media query in source/styles.css), while A's table relies on horizontal overflow scroll with min-width:640px and no visible scroll affordance, cutting off two of three plan columns at 390px — a direct miss against the brief's acceptance check that plan differences must remain legible. 2. B's headline claim always shows both the monthly and annual totals for the entered team size ($420/month or $4,200/year for 35 members) so the exact Team cost is visible without toggling or mental arithmetic, and the same claim self-disqualifies Team (claim-disqualified state, verified in source) when seat count exceeds the 100-member cap; A only shows the currently selected cadence and its Team price card has no such disqualification logic for over-cap sizes (verified by absence of an overCap branch in renderTeamPricing()). 3. B gives the Enterprise path — one of the two 'appropriate next actions' named in the brief — an actionable Contact Sales button with a captured click-confirmation state, while A presents 'Contact sales' as static text with no interactive affordance.
suspected_unblinding: none — file names, comments, and README scaffolding text in both packets read as independent, hand-authored implementations with no identifying builder or tool signals.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The 'Plan differences' table does not restructure for narrow viewports. It sits in a .table-scroll (overflow-x:auto) container with table min-width:640px and no responsive breakpoint that reflows it, so at the required 390px viewport only the Detail and Starter columns are visible; Team and Enterprise are pushed off-screen with only a text sliver showing and no visible scroll cue in the screenshot. This directly conflicts with the acceptance check that plan differences, limits, billing cadence, and cancellation terms remain legible.

text node with no href/button/click handler, unlike the Team card's explicit 'Start a Team trial' button. Since the brief states the appropriate next action for an undecided visitor is 'to start a trial or contact sales,' the second of those two actions has no affordance to actually perform it.

findings.label: A
findings.description: renderTeamPricing() computes and displays a Team per-member price and total for any entered member count with no over-cap branch; only the separate 'Which plan fits' recommendation text (not the price claim itself) tells an over-100-member visitor Team doesn't fit. Not demonstrated in the provided screenshots (default input is 35), but the gap is visible in source and would let an over-cap visitor see a live-looking Team price on the primary price claim.

findings.label: A
findings.description: CSS defines a visible :focus-visible outline on the billing radios, but the evidence capture script exercises the 'keyboard interaction' state via page.focus() + ArrowRight (a programmatic focus call) rather than a real Tab press, and the resulting screenshot shows no visible focus ring on either pill. Real Tab-order reachability of the control is not demonstrated by the supplied evidence.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The primary 'Start Team Trial' / 'Contact Sales' call-to-action buttons and the inline field-error text both use the same red hue, reducing the color's usefulness as a distinct semantic signal for errors versus primary actions in a persuade/decision context.
